questions.question:
The Pod `bar` in the namespace `web-logs` checks a list of websites and logs the result.

Extract the log lines of `bar` that contain the error `unable-to-access-website` and write **only those lines** to `/tmp/exam/q1/bar-errors.log` on `cka-q1`.

verification.description: bar-errors.log holds exactly the matching log lines

questions.question:
Check how many nodes of the cluster are `Ready` **and** can run normal workloads, i.e. do not carry a taint with the effect `NoSchedule`.

Write only that number to `/tmp/exam/q2/schedulable-nodes.txt` on `cka-q2`.

verification.description: schedulable-nodes.txt holds the right number

questions.question:
Pods can resolve the names of cluster Services, but every lookup of an external name (for example `kubernetes.io`) times out.

Investigate and repair CoreDNS so that Pods resolve external names again through the resolvers of the node (`/etc/resolv.conf`). Cluster names must keep working.

The Pod `dns-client` in the namespace `dns-repair` can be used for testing, e.g. `kubectl exec -n dns-repair dns-client -- nslookup kubernetes.io`.

verification.description: CoreDNS forwards external names to the node's resolvers
Cluster and external names resolve from a Pod

questions.question:
Workloads need to reach an internal service by the name `myapp.internal`, which is not in any DNS zone.

Configure CoreDNS so that a lookup of `myapp.internal` from any Pod returns the IP address `10.10.10.10`. Resolution of all other names must keep working.

The Pod `dns-client` in the namespace `dns-custom` can be used for testing.

verification.description: CoreDNS configuration maps myapp.internal
myapp.internal resolves to 10.10.10.10 from a Pod

questions.question:
In the namespace `lookup`, the Deployment `nginx-random` runs nginx on port `80`.

1. Expose it with a `ClusterIP` Service `nginx-random` on port `80`.
2. From a temporary Pod with the image `busybox:1.36`, look up the DNS name of the Service and save the `nslookup` output to `/tmp/exam/q5/nginx-random.svc` on `cka-q5`.
3. From a temporary Pod, look up the DNS name of one `nginx-random` **Pod** and save the `nslookup` output to `/tmp/exam/q5/nginx-random.pod`.

verification.description: Service nginx-random on port 80 with endpoints
Service lookup saved to nginx-random.svc
Pod lookup saved to nginx-random.pod

questions.question:
The spec file `/tmp/exam/q6/ledger.yaml` on `cka-q6` defines the Pod `ledger` (namespace `init-lab`). Its container exits if the file `/workdir/ready.flag` does not exist.

1. Add an init container named `prepare` (image `busybox:1.36`) that creates the empty file `/workdir/ready.flag` in the Pod's existing `workdir` volume.
2. Save your changes in `/tmp/exam/q6/ledger.yaml`, then create the Pod from that file.

The Pod must be `Running` and its container must not have restarted.

verification.description: ledger.yaml has an init container mounting workdir at /workdir
Pod ledger runs after its init container created ready.flag

questions.question:
In the namespace `secret-lab`:

1. Create a Secret `app-secret` with the key `password` and the value `n0t-s0-s3cret`.
2. Create a Pod `secret-file` (image `nginx:1.27`) that mounts the Secret as files in the directory `/secrets`.
3. Create a Pod `secret-env` (image `nginx:1.27`) that exposes the key `password` of the Secret as the environment variable `APP_PASSWORD`.

verification.description: Secret app-secret with the right password
secret-file reads the password from /secrets/password
secret-env has APP_PASSWORD from the Secret

questions.question:
The Deployment `cms` in the namespace `blog` must run `3` replicas on the node `k3d-cluster-agent-1`, but none of its Pods can be scheduled.

Adjust the resource **requests** so that the node's resources are shared evenly by the 3 Pods, leaving some headroom for the node and its other Pods:

- each Pod requests between `20%` and `30%` of the node's **allocatable** CPU and memory
- the init container and the `cms` container use exactly the same requests
- keep the node selector; you don't need to set limits

All 3 replicas must be running. (Tip: scaling the Deployment to `0` while you edit it can help.)

verification.description: Requests are 20-30% of the node's allocatable, identical in both containers
3 replicas of cms are ready

questions.question:
In the namespace `oneoff`, run a Pod named `envdump` with the image `busybox:1.36` that prints its environment variables (`env`) once.

Save the output to `/tmp/exam/q9/env.txt` on `cka-q9`. The Pod must not exist anymore when you are done.

verification.description: env.txt holds the environment of envdump
The Pod envdump was removed

questions.question:
A Helm chart for the edge proxy is in `/tmp/exam/q10/edge-proxy` on `cka-q10`.

Install it as the release `edge` in the namespace `edge` (create it), with the proxy's support for the **Kubernetes Gateway API** enabled. Look at the chart's values to find the setting; keep the Ingress support enabled.

Do not edit the chart: set the value at install time.

verification.description: Release edge of edge-proxy is deployed in edge
Gateway API provider enabled through values

questions.question:
In the namespace `limits-lab`, create a LimitRange `container-limits` so that:

- containers that set no resources get the requests `cpu: 100m`, `memory: 50Mi` and the limits `cpu: 200m`, `memory: 100Mi`
- no container can have a memory limit above `500Mi`

Test it, for example with `kubectl run test -n limits-lab --image=nginx:1.27 --dry-run=server -o yaml`.

verification.description: LimitRange container-limits with the right defaults and maximum
Defaults applied and the 500Mi maximum enforced

questions.question:
Several PersistentVolumes carry the label `team=storage-audit`.

List **only those** PersistentVolumes, **sorted by capacity** from smallest to largest, using `kubectl get` with its default columns, and save the output to `/tmp/exam/q12/pv-by-size.txt` on `cka-q12`.

verification.description: The storage-audit PVs are listed from smallest to largest
The output has the default kubectl get columns

questions.question:
Show that a `Retain` reclaim policy keeps data after its claim is deleted:

1. Create a StorageClass `keep-local` with the provisioner `rancher.io/local-path`, the reclaim policy `Retain` and the binding mode `WaitForFirstConsumer`. It must not be the default StorageClass.
2. In the namespace `retain-lab`, create a PVC `scratch` (`64Mi`, `ReadWriteOnce`, StorageClass `keep-local`) and a Pod `writer` (image `busybox:1.36`) that mounts it at `/data` and writes the text `hello from writer` to `/data/hello.txt`.
3. Once the file is written, delete the Pod `writer` and the PVC `scratch`.

The PersistentVolume that was provisioned for `scratch` must still exist afterwards, with its data.

verification.description: StorageClass keep-local (local-path, Retain, WaitForFirstConsumer)
The PV of scratch is Released, PVC and Pod deleted
hello.txt is still on the retained volume

questions.question:
The platform team runs the Gateway `shared-gw` (class `shared-gw-class`) in the namespace `infra`. Its listener `http` (port `80`) currently accepts routes only from its own namespace. There is no gateway controller, so only the resources are graded.

Expose the Service `web-service` (namespace `web-app`, port `80`) through `shared-gw` for the host `web.example.com`:

1. Allow the listener `http` to accept routes from namespaces labeled `gateway-access=true` (not from all namespaces), and label the namespace `web-app` accordingly.
2. Create an HTTPRoute `web-route` in `web-app`, attached to `shared-gw`, that sends `web.example.com` to `web-service` on port `80`.

verification.description: Listener http accepts routes from gateway-access=true namespaces; web-app labeled
HTTPRoute web-route attached to infra/shared-gw

questions.question:
Write a report of the Pods in the namespace `audit-lab` to `/tmp/exam/q15/pod-status.txt` on `cka-q15`, using `kubectl` with **custom columns**:

- column `POD_NAME`: the Pod name
- column `POD_STATUS`: the Pod's phase (`.status.phase`)
- rows sorted by Pod name

The file must contain the header line and one line per Pod.

verification.description: pod-status.txt lists every Pod with its phase, sorted by name
